Do I need _proc in my Github project?

🤖Reply🤖

⏳ web_search(type="search", queries="['site:nbdev.fast.ai _proc nbdev', 'site…", query="site:nbdev.fast.ai _proc nbdev") ⏳

No—assuming _proc/ is the directory generated by nbdev, you normally should not commit it to GitHub.
It contains intermediate, preprocessed notebooks and Quarto files used to build or preview documentation. nbdev recreates it as needed, so add this to .gitignore:
_proc/
Keep your source notebooks, exported package, configuration, and other hand-authored files under version control. _proc/ is mainly useful locally for debugging documentation processing or publishing through Quarto. (nbdev.fast.ai)*
{"model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "prompt_tokens": 48125, "completion_tokens": 289, "total_tokens": 48414, "cached_tokens": 41600, "reasoning_tokens": 155, "cost": 0.007435500000000001}
Can I remove the whole thing to fix?


🤖Reply🤖
Yes. You can safely delete the entire _proc/ directory; nbdev will regenerate it during the next docs build.
From the project root:
rm -rf _proc
nbdev_docs
If the problem persists, _proc/ was not the underlying cause—the source notebook or docs configuration likely needs fixing. Keep _proc/ excluded from Git:
_proc/

title: BasedTab
text:
Install latest from the GitHub repository:
$ pip install git+https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/BasedTab.git
or from conda
$ conda install -c AnswerDotAI BasedTab
or from pypi
$ pip install BasedTab
